steps.body: Apply the idea in a new form.

widget.prompt: Add 3.5 and 4.65. Pad 3.5 as 3.50 first, so the columns line up. What is the sum?

commonErrors.feedback: That read 3.5 as 3.05, dropping the 5 into the hundredths place instead of padding it into the tenths place — 3.5 is 3.50, not 3.05.
5 + 6 was added as 10 instead of 11, so the tenths digit was written as 0 — that is 0.10 short of 8.15.

widget.prompt: Subtracting 5.2 − 1.47, what does writing 5.2 as 5.20 do?

options.label: It fills the hundredths place
options.feedback: Correct — a trailing zero adds no amount, but it fills the column so the subtraction has somewhere to work.

options.label: It makes 5.2 larger
options.feedback: 5.20 and 5.2 are exactly equal; the zero adds no hundredths at all.

options.label: It rounds the number up
options.feedback: Nothing is rounded — the value is untouched, only the way it is written changes.

options.label: It is not allowed
options.feedback: It is standard practice, and it is what makes ragged-length subtraction workable.
